source_passage_locator: K053S01: NIDDK High Blood Pressure & Kidney Disease → How does high blood pressure affect the kidneys? → First paragraph describing narrowing, damage and weakening of renal blood vessels
review_note: Reviewed K053S01. NIDDK explicitly explains that high blood pressure constricts and narrows blood vessels, eventually damaging and weakening them throughout the body, including in the kidneys. The narrowing reduces blood flow. This directly supports Longstanding high blood pressure → Damage and narrowing of kidney blood vessels as a possible causal mechanism. Not every hypertensive patient develops renal vascular injury. AI-assisted review; human confirmation pending.

effect_node: Reduced renal filtration and chronic kidney disease
source_passage_locator: K053S02: NIDDK High Blood Pressure & Kidney Disease → How does high blood pressure affect the kidneys? → Both paragraphs describing vessel narrowing and damage, impaired renal waste and fluid removal, and progressive kidney dysfunction
review_note: Reviewed K053S02 and SRC008. K053S02 directly establishes that narrowed and damaged renal blood vessels can lose normal function, reducing the kidneys' ability to remove waste and excess fluid. The article also identifies hypertension as a cause of kidney disease and describes progressive injury that can lead to kidney failure. This supports Damage and narrowing of kidney blood vessels → Reduced renal filtration and chronic kidney disease as a possible causal pathway. SRC008 independently describes vessel and filtering-system damage leading to impaired filtration but does not explicitly establish vessel narrowing; its exact-link review remains partial and it is excluded from supporting_source_ids. Reduced filtration alone does not establish chronic kidney disease without evidence of chronicity. AI-assisted review; human confirmation pending.
